questions.note: The cascade is right: the hallux leads, toe 2 is close behind, 3 to 5 step back and the 5th lies small against the 4th. The modelling gives it away, though. The lesser toes are straight, parallel cylinders with ring-band knuckles and dark clefts down to the webs (plan, V5f). From below they are stacked pills (V4), and a slit separates the hallux from toe 2 (V4o). Little pulp bulge.

The scan's ankle reads real. The lateral malleolus sits lower and further back with its hollow, and the Achilles is a clear cord with hollows either side in V8. The medial malleolus is only a faint swell in V2 and V8. In V8 a broad extra column fills the medial side and spoils the read. No anterior ankle crease shows in V1f, V2 or V3.

defects.what: From above the toes are separate cylindrical shafts with ring-band knuckles and dark clefts nearly to the webs. A dark slot runs along the base between the hallux and toe 2, so the row reads as a hand's fingers, where the scan's toes press together.
defects.fix: Close the clefts so the lesser toes touch side by side and broaden their bases. Soften the knuckle rings into low dorsal swells and lay the hallux against toe 2 with no slot.

defects.what: From below, toes 2 to 4 are parallel cylinders cut by crisp transverse ring creases, like stacked pills, and the 5th is a crumpled knot. The scan beside it shows plump rounded pads behind a soft sulcus.
defects.fix: Give each plantar toe one domed pulp pad and a soft flexion crease or two. Let the pads widen and touch, sitting behind a continuous toe sulcus as in the scan.

defects.what: From behind, a broad second mass fills the frame beyond the heel's medial edge, far outside the scan's ankle outline. The heel then sits under the lateral half of the column and the medial malleolus is lost against it.
defects.fix: Make the medial side of the ankle end where the scan's does, a malleolus-width outside the heel, or hide whatever other geometry stands there in this view.

defects.what: The plantar silhouette has a narrow, deep slit between the hallux and toe 2 that runs up to the web and ends in a pinched spike. The two toes should touch; they should not stand apart along their length.
defects.fix: Close the gap so the hallux and toe 2 meet along their sides, with only a shallow groove at the web.

defects.what: The extensor tendons are five or six thin, crisp, evenly spaced ridges from the ankle to the toes. They are the sharpest relief on the foot, so the scan's soft dorsal dome reads engraved with cables.
defects.fix: Real extensor cords on a relaxed foot are low, broad and blurred into the dome. Only the hallux's shows clearly. Lower and widen the rest and fade them out over the metatarsals.

defects.what: From the side, the 5th toe ends at its base in a hard vertical ring, like a capped tube. The tips of the other toes carry crimped rims and creases, where the scan's toes are smooth rounded beads.
defects.fix: Blend the 5th toe's base into the forefoot with a soft fold. Round the tips into pulp bulges under the nails, with no sharp rims.

defects.what: The back of the ankle's silhouette steps in with a small kink about 110 mm up, in the zone where the scan's shape eases into the model's own leg. Two shapes meet there instead of one smooth Achilles curve.
defects.fix: Ease the blend over a longer band so the posterior outline keeps continuous curvature from the heel up into the leg.

defects.what: A short, straight, sharp slit crosses the hallux's plantar pad and reads as a knife cut, not a skin crease.
defects.fix: A real interphalangeal crease is a shallow, slightly curved fold with soft lips; make it wider and less deep.

defects.what: Small sharp slits and ticks sit at the roots of the 2-3, 3-4 and 4-5 webs. They read as mesh pinches, not soft skin folds.
defects.fix: Round the web roots into shallow U-shaped commissures with no hard edge.

defects.what: Concentric, contour-like ripples cover the back of the hallux behind the nail fold, like a displacement artefact. A real joint has two or three transverse interphalangeal wrinkles instead.
defects.fix: Replace the rings with a few transverse wrinkles over the joint, of uneven length and depth.

defects.what: The lateral toes that show past the heel from behind carry crinkled, crimped ridges like crumpled plastic. The scan's toes in the same place are smooth beads.

ranked: [D1] From above the toes are a hand's fingers: separate shafts with bead knuckles and dark clefts to the webs, with a slot along the hallux. A man's toes press together, broadest at the bases, as in the scan beside them.
[D2] From below, the toes are stacked pills with crisp ring creases. Real plantar toes are one plump pad each, behind a soft sulcus.

Two methods show: the scanned body is soft and organic, but the modelled toes and dorsal relief are crisp, regular and hard-edged. Detail is sharp in those places and soft everywhere else, so the foot reads stitched together.
[D3] From behind, a broad mass stands outside the heel's medial edge, beyond the scan's outline. The ankle reads off-centre over the heel and the medial malleolus disappears into it.
[D5] The dorsum carries thin, even, crisp tendon cords that read as cables on a smooth dome. A relaxed foot shows one clear hallux tendon and soft, blurred ridges for the others.
The declared vein relief hides the dorsum's large form. In V1f the venous arch crosses the instep as one hard line like a strap seam, and in V2o it nicks the instep silhouette.
[D4] In the plantar silhouette, a narrow slit with a spike at its top separates the hallux from toe 2. The declaration has them touching.
[D6] From the side, the 5th toe ends in a hard ring like a capped tube, and the other tips are crimped. The scan's toes are smooth rounded beads there.
The lesser toes in V5f are straight, parallel and flat-topped, with the nail on the very tip. Real lesser toes are short, flex down at the joints and have a pulp that bulges past the nail.
[D7] The posterior ankle outline kinks about 110 mm up, where the scan eases into the model's leg: a step where two shapes meet.
No anterior ankle crease reads at the front of the ankle in V1f, V2 or V3. A real foot shows a soft fold there at the dorsiflexion line.
The medial malleolus is only a faint swell in V2 and V8, while the lateral one is a clear knob, so the ankle reads one-sided. This is as in the scan, but a lean man's medial dome usually shows.
Above about 150 mm the leg in V2 and V3 is a perfectly straight, smooth tube. The scanned ankle looks grafted onto a mannequin shin.
[D8] A straight, sharp slit across the hallux's plantar pad reads as a cut, not a crease.
[D9] Sharp slits sit at the roots of the lesser toes' webs, like mesh pinches.
[D10] Contour-like ripple rings sit on the back of the hallux, a displacement artefact rather than interphalangeal wrinkles.
[D11] The lateral toes that show behind the heel in V8 are crinkled like crumpled plastic.
